title: Why Did Ten People Vanish from an Intact Ship in 1872? | Curiosity Case Files｜ CC字幕
description:
In 1872, all ten people vanished from the Mary Celeste while her sails and cargo remained.
For viewers separating ghost-ship facts from later additions.

The first Curiosity Case Files dossier compares 150 years of tavern stories—hot food, all boats aboard, sea monsters and the Bermuda Triangle—with the December 1872 records. Dei Gratia's chief mate saw sails and bilge water; the boat and navigation tools were missing, but 1,701 alcohol barrels and six months of provisions remained. Three months in Gibraltar's Vice-Admiralty Court brought the attorney general's murder theory, sword marks that looked like blood, tests, and salvage worth about a fifth of the estimated ship and cargo value.

Seven explanations face three questions: the earliest source, who spoke and in what setting, and what each explains or leaves unexplained. We show the best-supported account and its gaps. We stick to the records, label later additions and state where no verdict exists. As of 2026-10-10; sources for numbers, dates and quotes are below.

AI-generated illustrations portray historical figures as cartoon characters, without recreating likenesses. Photos are public-domain archives; see image credits.

9wsg.text: Sails still set, the ship moved on. The boat stayed at sea, farther behind.

nhz6.text: A 2007 weather reconstruction found she sailed herself for those nine days.

bwmh.text: This has gaps too: why take the sextant and papers for a temporary exit?

4f9b.text: The boat and ten people were never found.

6azw.text: In 1885, a new captain ran her onto a Haitian reef for insurance fraud.

u2ek.text: She didn't sink. The fraud was exposed; the jury deadlocked seven to five.

nrsd.text: Back to our question: they didn't vanish; they couldn't get back.

mnjn.text: Ten people, one boat, nine empty barrels. The records end without a verdict.
